clue.text: A thing you talk about, like an allergic reaction

parts.note: a topic is a subject of conversation

explanation.surface: A conversation subject compared to an allergic flare-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Atopic is the medical adjective for a hereditary tendency to allergies such as eczema and hay fever.

clue.text: Duck leaves lake

parts.note: tea leaves, so leaves can stand for tea
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A duck flies away from the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb but is a noun: the leaves brewed as tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater dabbling duck.

clue.text: Choose one of the players for the ride

parts.note: to choose is to pick
one gives the article A
a back is one of the players in a football or rugby team

explanation.surface: Selecting one team member to get a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickaback is an older word for a piggyback, a ride carried on someone's back.

clue.text: Man who knows about joints? More or less a dropout

parts.note: c, short for Latin circa, means about or roughly
a hippy is a stereotypical dropout from conventional society

explanation.surface: Someone expert in joints, suggesting cannabis, is pretty much a dropout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joints' hints at cannabis and so at the hippy, but the joints are woodwork. CHIPPY is British slang for a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter, British slang chippy, is an expert in making wooden joints.

clue.text: Sexist description thus to upset females?

indicators.note: upset tells us to knock the letters of thus to out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A remark asking whether a sexist label is meant to annoy women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the sexist remark's effect on women, but 'to upset' is the anagram signal; FF is just plural females.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a sexually attractive person in this way is an objectifying, sexist phrase.

clue.text: It's Rod/Pam, him/her mixed up in this?

definitions.text: It's Rod/Pam, him/her mixed up in this?

indicators.note: mixed up tells us to jumble every letter of the names and pronouns before it

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person who is Rod and Pam, him and her, all jumbled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Having both male and female sexual characteristics is exactly being both him and her at once.

clue.text: The answer interwoven with a number of strands

indicators.note: interwoven suggests threads crossing each other, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
an answer is a reply

explanation.surface: A response woven together out of many strands of thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Wool or yarn described this way is made of three twisted strands, a specific number.

clue.text: Leaders in the event making very good speeds

indicators.note: the leaders of a run of words are their opening letters

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: The top competitors at a meeting are setting excellent speeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, a musical speed.

clue.text: Possibly Chinese food at the back

parts.note: fare is food served
astern means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Perhaps a Chinese takeaway eaten at the rear of the room.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies in the Far East, so Chinese is an example of something from that region.

clue.text: Less regular one going to church embraced by Father

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside the word for father

parts.note: pater is Latin, used in English, for father

indicators.note: going to puts one after the church abbreviation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An irregular worshipper heads to church and is hugged by the priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less regular' hides an adjective, not a churchgoer: an irregular attender is the surface trap. 'going to' and 'embraced by' build the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something patchier is more uneven or inconsistent, hence less regular.

clue.text: Comment about student's achievement?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a mark is the score a student achieves

explanation.surface: A teacher's remark on how well a student has done.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a spoken or written comment.

clue.text: Begins to show such order

parts.note: the opening letters A, B, C start the sequence of words ordered by the letters they begin with

explanation.surface: Something starts to display a certain sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering by initial letters, A then B then C, is the dictionary arrangement of the letter sequence.

clue.text: Released from Premiership team: fellow that's upset another

parts.note: Man U is short for Manchester United, an English Premier League football club

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the fellow's name over

parts.note: Tim is a man's name, a fellow
Ted is another man's name

explanation.surface: A footballer freed from his club, upset by another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's upset' turns TIM into MIT. Man U is Manchester United, a Premier League football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To manumit is to free a slave, so manumitted means released from bondage.

clue.text: Male ace establishes authority

parts.note: a man is a male
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A top man asserts his dominance.
explanation.definitionFit: Mana is power or prestige, originally a Polynesian idea of authority.

clue.text: Fools semi-wild or semi-nuts?

definitions.meaning: someone half crazy, playfully described as possessing only a half share of reason

explanation.surface: Idiots are half crazy or partly mad.
explanation.walkthrough: There is also a reverse reading: half of WITS is WI, half of wild, or TS, half of nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Halfwits are foolish people, those supposedly with only half their wits.

clue.text: Bridge designer lacking a thing that could give the edge

definitions.text: thing that could give the edge

indicators.note: lacking tells us a letter is missing from the inventor's name

parts.note: Charles Wheatstone devised the Wheatstone bridge, an electrical measuring circuit

explanation.surface: A bridge engineer is missing something that would give him an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests a river crossing, but the Wheatstone bridge is an electrical circuit named after the Victorian scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpening stone puts the edge back on blades, a literal sense of giving the edge.

clue.text: Academic dean sacked, treated with no respect

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic

indicators.note: sacked suggests the dean thrown about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A college dean is fired and treated with contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Profaned means desecrated, treating something sacred without reverence.

clue.text: Cowboy to jump up on an unrideable hopper?

parts.note: to buck is to leap upward, as a horse does
roo is short for kangaroo, a hopper nobody rides

explanation.surface: A cowboy leaps onto a kangaroo that cannot be ridden.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckaroo is an American word for a cowboy.

clue.text: Jane finally married in gooey read

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Jane gets wed at last in a sentimental novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Eyre, Charlotte Bronte's heroine, does finally marry Rochester.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel bears this surname, and she ends the book married.

clue.text: Affected elegance that comes with casual greeting

parts.note: chic means stylish elegance
hi is an informal hello

explanation.surface: Stylishness that comes with a breezy hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichi describes something pretentiously fussy or showy, which is affected style.

clue.text: British hurt by old horrors — liberal legislation needed

parts.note: ill means harmed or hurt
frights are horrors or scares

explanation.surface: British people damaged by past terrors need liberal laws.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute guaranteeing citizens' freedoms is legislation that is liberal in spirit.

clue.text: Don't bother about holidays

explanation.definitionFit: To leave something is to not bother with it, and leave is also authorised time off.

clue.text: Ritual only 50% completed? One's waxy

indicators.note: only half done means the second half of the ritual word is cut away

parts.note: a ceremony is a ritual

explanation.surface: A ceremony only half finished; one is waxy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only 50% completed' keeps the first four letters of CEREMONY.
explanation.definitionFit: The cere is the waxy-looking swelling at the base of some birds' beaks.

clue.text: Race demands big effort

explanation.surface: A race calls for a lot of exertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a breed or line of descent, and also a severe exertion.

clue.text: Inclusive paramour doing very nicely

parts.note: inc is an abbreviation for inclusive
a paramour is a lover

explanation.surface: An all-embracing lover is thriving.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means living in comfort and prosperity, which is doing very well.

clue.text: Extra reading matter tot gets to finish with hesitation

parts.note: to tot up is to add
an end is a finish
um is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A toddler hesitates before finishing a book's extra pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child, but it is the verb meaning to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is extra material added to the end of a book.

clue.text: Pasquale can have extreme anxiety, would you believe it?

parts.note: the setter Pasquale refers to himself, I
a fever is a state of nervous excitement

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to great nervousness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of surprise, as in 'if ever there was one', expressing disbelief.
